findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Scope section with AC4: either amend Scope to 'Read-only analysis; the only write is a single comment appended to this ticket upon completion,' or move the findings-recording mechanism outside the ticket store (e.g., a local artifact) so the Scope claim remains accurate.
evidence: Scope: 'Read-only analysis of the rebar ticket store; no repository files will be modified.'
AC4: 'Findings are recorded on this ticket; verified by the presence of the final analysis comment.'

src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py:47 — `def comment(ticket_id, body, ...)` appends a COMMENT event; src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:37 — 'comment': _Cmd(leaf.comment, ...) — writing a comment is a store-mutating operation.
ABSENCE: the Scope section does not carve out the comment-write as an exception to the read-only claim.
findings.finding: The plan's Scope section declares 'Read-only analysis of the rebar ticket store; no repository files will be modified,' yet AC4 requires a write operation — appending a comment to this ticket — to satisfy 'Findings are recorded on this ticket; verified by the presence of the final analysis comment.' These two statements directly contradict each other: AC4's deliverable is a mutation of the ticket store, which the Scope section explicitly forbids.
findings.location: Scope section ('Read-only analysis... no repository files will be modified') vs. AC4 ('Findings are recorded on this ticket; verified by the presence of the final analysis comment')
scenarios: An executor reading the Scope literally treats the ticket store as read-only throughout and never writes the AC4 comment — AC4 becomes unverifiable and the ticket cannot be closed.
An executor writes the comment to satisfy AC4 but is then in violation of the declared Scope, leaving reviewers uncertain whether the read-only constraint was actually respected during the analysis.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Scope section to: 'Read-only analysis of the rebar ticket store; the only mutation is a single COMMENT appended to this ticket recording the findings. No other repository files or ticket store entries will be modified.'

findings.finding: The plan's entire subject matter rests on 'the proposed deterministic clarity criteria,' but these criteria are never named, enumerated, linked, or pointed to by file path or ticket ID anywhere in the plan. Every acceptance criterion refers to 'each proposed criterion' or 'each criterion,' making this a load-bearing precondition. A Grep/Read of the repo for 'proposed deterministic clarity criteria,' 'clarity criteria,' 'retain narrow advisory,' and 'counterexample false positive rule' returns zero hits. An agent executing this plan has no way to locate the criteria it is supposed to validate.
findings.location: Context / Problem; Acceptance Criteria (all four ACs reference 'each proposed criterion' or 'each criterion')
scenarios: An executing agent cannot search for counterexamples to criteria that are never identified — the plan's work is entirely blocked on this missing input.
Without the criteria enumerated, the AC verification step ('verified by a structured recommendation table') cannot be completed because the rows of the table are undefined.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Prerequisites / Inputs' section that either (a) lists each criterion inline by name/description, or (b) cites the ticket or file (e.g. `[rebar:<ID>]`) that defines them, so the criteria are unambiguously reachable before any search work begins.

findings.finding: The Approach section asserts 'Search completed and accepted tickets' as if the rebar ticket store exposes a status-filtered corpus, but no evidence confirms that 'completed' or 'accepted' status filtering is available via the rebar search interface. The confirmed rebar subcommands (show, list, deps, ready, next-batch, search) do not document a status-filter syntax anywhere in the repo, leaving this premise unverifiable.

scenarios: If rebar search does not support status filtering, the agent must manually inspect every returned ticket to determine whether it was accepted — making the 'search completed and accepted tickets' approach unreliable or impractical.
If 'accepted' is not a tracked rebar status value, the filtering premise is doubly unverifiable.
